sample.title: The Truth About How Data Centers Use Water And Power To Keep Cool
sample.description:
U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.

sample.title: LIVE: House votes on Hegseth impeachment next steps — 11/10/2026
sample.description:
The House is set to vote Tuesday on a procedural motion related to the Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth impeachment resolution. If it passes, the measure will proceed to a debate and vote. Impeachment resolutions are privileged, meaning the House must act on them, table them or vote to refer them to committee within two legislative days.

Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth on Tuesday railed against the Republican congressman who introduced articles of impeachment against him and aggressively defended his leadership in the Iran war and other military operations.

“What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle, a personal manifesto driven by ego and resentment,” Hegseth said a day after Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., put forward the eight impeachment articles.

“It’s a farce, and it’s a stunt, and everybody knows it,” Hegseth said during his first Pentagon news conference in six months.

I was accused of spying for China | BBC News
sample.description:
In his first interview, parliamentary researcher Chris Cash has spoken to the BBC about being accused of spying for China. 

In 2023 Chris Cash and his friend - Chris Berry - were arrested on suspicion of spying for China, but last year the case was suddenly dropped and the pair were acquitted.

Prosecutors said the case was dropped because the government wouldn’t confirm that China was an ‘enemy’ of the UK. 

Chris Cash has given the BBC thousands of messages he exchanged with Chris Berry  between January 2022 and March 2023, which were at the heart of the prosecution’s case.

BBC Politics Investigations Correspondent Joe Pike analyses the messages and asks Chris Cash how information from inside parliament may have reached the upper echelons of the Chinese Communist Party. 

Chris Berry does not want to comment on this story. But he’s previously denied wrongdoing and said he’s been unfairly subjected to a trial by media, he believed his ex-employer had clients wishing to develop trading links with the UK, and his work contained no classified information. 

The Chinese Embassy in London has previously called these allegations “completely fabricated and nothing but malicious slander”.
